name: Fighting Techniques
body:
A bravo learns fighting techniques by studying with another or on his own, in order to better take advantage of his opponent and the terrain. Below are five of the most popular techniques, identified by the name of the sword master who developed it and the animal that symbolize it’s spirit. At 1st level, he selects one of the following fighting techniques. He learns additional techniques as he gains levels in the bravo class.

The bravo gains a bonus to a number of capabilities while in either form. The use of a fighting technique is automatically be noticed by a creature with a base attack bonus equal to or greater than the bravo. A fighting technique automatically ends if the bravo is immobilized or helpless.

There are five basic fighting techniques written to be simple and neatly fit in a small space, and to not have special exceptions or clauses on how to use them. Other techniques are a bit more complex and do not follow the same rules as the basic ones, but have the same general power level.

Basic Techniques
Broile (Cobra)

Passive Form: Climb, Swim

Focused Form: Critical confirmation rolls

Debilitating Effect: Sickened

Eduke (Wolf)

Passive Form: Disguise, Knowledge (local)

Focused Form: Combat maneuver bonus

Debilitating Effect: –4 penalty to AC

Fahrns (Lion)

Passive Form: Diplomacy, Intimidate

Focused Form: Damage rolls

Debilitating Effect: Shaken

Macahn (Fox)

Passive Form: Bluff, Sense Motive

Focused Form: Saving throws

Debilitating Effect: Cannot make attacks of opportunity

Silveri (Hare)

Passive Form: Acrobatics, Escape Artist

Focused Form: Increase the bravo’s speed by 5-feet per +1 bonus.

Debilitating Effect: Fatigued

Complex Techniques
Russelvar (Bear)

Passive Form: Knowledge (nobility), Perception

Focused Form: The bravo gains 2 temporary hit point at the beginning of each turn. These temporary hit points do not stack. At 6th level and every six levels thereafter this number of temporary hit points he gains increases by 1.

Debilitating Effect: The target suffers bleed damage equal to the bravo’s level at the beginning of each turn. This bleeding can be stopped by a successful Heal skill check (DC = 10 + 1/2 the bravo’s level + his Intelligence modifier) or through the application of any magical healing.

Origametti (Crane)

Passive Form: Craft (any one), Heal

Focused Form: Once per turn when the bravo scores a critical hit, the target takes 1 point of Dexterity ability damage. Beginning at 12th level, the target instead takes 2 points of Dexterity ability damage.

Debilitating Effect: The target cannot use one extraordinary or supernatural ability chosen by the bravo. The bravo must have seen the target use the ability or have previously made a successful Knowledge check to identity the ability.

Edwin (Horse)

Passive Form: Ride and initiative checks

Focused Form: All Dexterity-based checks

Debilitating Effect: The target suffers a –2 penalty to attacks, initiative, Acrobatics, Fly, Perception, and Swim Checks. The target also takes a 10 foot penalty to the speed of it’s primary form of movement.

Herpestid (Mongoose)

Passive Form: all saving throws against poison

Focused Form: All Dexterity-based checks

Debilitating Effect: The target’s base speed is reduced by half.

Highcrest (Falcon)

Passive Form: Fly, Perception

Focused Form: Attack and damage rolls with projectile ranged weapons. While using this technique, the bravo does not gain the usual bonus to AC and attacks with bravo weapons.

Debilitating Effect: the target suffers a –2 penalty to ranged attacks and a –10 to Perception checks that rely on sight. While using this technique, the bravo can use debilitating attack with  projectile ranged weapons instead of bravo weapons. If he is using more than one fighting technique, such as allowed by the master of five styles class feature, he can use either.
